links.note: Was on 32901 UNESCO and Vedic Chanting, which is about oral transmission and the seers. The belief that the deities are ultimately one is stated in 32902 - the early rishis and rishikas saw those gods and goddesses as one, not separate beings, ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti.
Was on 32901 UNESCO and Vedic Chanting. Janas as the clans or larger groups of people, with the Bharatas, Purus, Kurus, Yadus and Turvashas named, is in 32902's account of Vedic society.
Was on 32901 UNESCO and Vedic Chanting. The Upanishads as the group of texts that built upon Vedic concepts and introduced rebirth and karma is stated in 32904.

Was on 32912 Ahimsa in Thought, and the Rock-Cut Caves, which mentions rock-cut caves in general. Ellora by name, with the caption that some of the caves are Hindu, others Buddhist and Jain, is in 32913, where the three traditions cut into the same hillside make the chapter's point.

Was on 32913 Schools of Thought, Not Religions, whose emphasis is on what the schools shared and on the word religion being too limiting. The statement the question needs is 32904's - other schools also emerged which did not accept the authority of the Vedas and developed their own systems, and one of them is Buddhism.
